title: Cohesion and Coupling
learningObjectives: Define cohesion and coupling in practical terms.
Recognize highly focused units of code.
Explain how cohesion and coupling affect change.
Suggest improvements to a poorly organized design.

understand.concept: Cohesion describes how closely the responsibilities inside a unit belong together. High cohesion means a function or module has a focused purpose. Coupling describes how much one unit depends on another. Lower unnecessary coupling means changes can be made with fewer ripple effects. Good design generally favors high cohesion and manageable coupling, while still allowing components to collaborate. These are design qualities, not absolute numeric targets; context and simplicity matter.
understand.whyItMatters: Focused responsibilities and controlled boundaries make software easier to change, test, and explain.
understand.analogy: A well-organized workshop keeps tools and tasks arranged so each job can be completed without disturbing unrelated work.
understand.analogyLimit: Real software components exchange data and have technical constraints that a physical workshop analogy cannot fully capture.

explain.narrative: A module that only formats dates has a cohesive purpose. If it also sends emails, updates inventory, and handles unrelated UI state, its cohesion is weak. If a component directly depends on many unrelated implementation details, coupling is high. Improve design by giving units clear responsibilities and passing only the information they need.

examples.title: Focused helper
examples.explanation: A single clear purpose gives the function high cohesion.

examples.title: Reduce needless dependency
examples.explanation: The function needs only a name, not a whole user record.

examples.title: Use a narrow interface
examples.explanation: Only the required values are passed.

examples.title: Recognize mixed responsibilities
examples.code:
function report(){console.log('calculate, save, send, display');}
report();
examples.explanation: The function name hints at several unrelated tasks that may need separation.

examples.title: Keep related operations together
examples.explanation: Related geometry calculations can live together in a focused module.

commonMistakes: Making boundaries too small or too large without a reason.
Allowing components to rely on hidden state.
Mixing unrelated responsibilities in one function.
Exposing internal data that callers can modify unexpectedly.
Treating a design guideline as a rigid rule instead of a contextual trade-off.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Inspect a unit that performs several unrelated tasks and depends on many values. List its responsibilities and dependencies. Group related responsibilities and remove unnecessary dependencies. Define a smaller input/output boundary. Explain whether cohesion improved and coupling was reduced.
steps: Inspect a unit that performs several unrelated tasks and depends on many values.
Group related responsibilities and remove unnecessary dependencies.
Explain whether cohesion improved and coupling was reduced.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Design a small inventory helper with add, remove, and count responsibilities. Keep related stock operations together. Avoid depending directly on UI or messaging services. Document its public inputs and outputs. Explain one way a future change would be isolated.
requirements: Design a small inventory helper with add, remove, and count responsibilities.
Avoid depending directly on UI or messaging services.
Document its public inputs and outputs.
Explain one way a future change would be isolated.

hints: Cohesion asks whether a unit's responsibilities belong together.
Coupling asks how much units depend on each other.
Aim for practical improvement, not a metric chase.

options: Responsibilities inside a unit closely fit its purpose
A unit has many unrelated tasks
Every unit imports every other unit
questions.answer: Responsibilities inside a unit closely fit its purpose
questions.explanation: Focused responsibilities make a unit easier to understand.
Coupling describes how strongly units depend on one another.

options: Focused units with limited necessary dependencies
Many units that know each other's internals
questions.answer: Focused units with limited necessary dependencies
questions.explanation: High cohesion and manageable coupling support maintainability.

options: Expose a narrow interface and pass required data
Make every function depend on UI
questions.answer: Expose a narrow interface and pass required data
questions.explanation: Narrow interfaces reduce dependence on implementation details.

questions.prompt: Are cohesion and coupling strict laws?
options: No; they are useful design qualities applied with context
questions.answer: No; they are useful design qualities applied with context
questions.explanation: They guide trade-offs rather than define rigid formulas.
